events.title: William Shakespeare is baptised
events.description: The infant William Shakespeare was baptised at Holy Trinity Church in Stratford-upon-Avon, England. His exact birth date is unrecorded, but the baptism is the earliest documented event of his life.
events.significance: The baptism date is the anchor for Shakespeare's biography. It is why his birthday is traditionally marked in late April.

events.title: John Wilkes Booth is cornered and killed
events.description: Union cavalry trapped Abraham Lincoln's assassin in a Virginia tobacco barn and shot him, ending a twelve-day manhunt. On the same day, Confederate General Joseph Johnston surrendered his army to General William T. Sherman near Durham, North Carolina.
events.significance: The two events closed the main chapters of the Civil War and the Lincoln assassination. Johnston's surrender was the largest of the war.

events.title: Guernica is bombed
events.description: During the Spanish Civil War, German aircraft bombed the ancient Basque town of Guernica in northern Spain.
events.significance: The attack became a global symbol of the horror of aerial bombardment of civilians. It inspired Picasso's famous painting Guernica.

events.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
events.description: A reactor exploded at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant in the Soviet Union. It released radioactive material across Europe.
events.significance: It is the worst nuclear power accident in history. It reshaped nuclear safety standards and public attitudes toward nuclear energy worldwide.
